primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Growth hormone excess after epiphyseal closure raises IGF-1 and causes soft-tissue and acral overgrowth, insulin resistance, and organ enlargement.
vignette: A 47-year-old man has increasing shoe size, coarse facial features, enlarged hands, headaches, and newly diagnosed diabetes.
distractor_notes: Cushing syndrome causes central obesity and catabolic features rather than acral enlargement.
Hypothyroidism can cause coarse features but not progressive hand and foot enlargement from GH excess.
Hyperparathyroidism causes calcium and bone abnormalities.
Prolactinoma causes reproductive dysfunction and galactorrhea rather than acral overgrowth.
key_expl: Adult-onset acral enlargement and coarse facial features strongly indicate growth hormone excess and acromegaly.
objective: Recognize acromegaly from characteristic adult GH excess.
clues: coarse facial features and enlarged hands

sources.title: Acromegaly
sources.support: NIDDK describes acromegaly as growth hormone excess in adults causing enlarged hands, feet, and facial changes.

sources.title: Acromegaly
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes acral and soft-tissue overgrowth from GH excess.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Deficient vasopressin secretion prevents collecting-duct water reabsorption; exogenous desmopressin restores urine concentrating ability.
vignette: After neurosurgery near the pituitary stalk, a patient develops polyuria, hypernatremia, and very dilute urine. Urine osmolality rises markedly after desmopressin.
distractor_notes: Aldosterone deficiency causes hyperkalemia and sodium loss, not isolated dilute polyuria corrected by desmopressin.
Cortisol deficiency causes adrenal insufficiency.
Insulin deficiency causes osmotic diuresis with glucosuria.
PTH regulates calcium and phosphate.
key_expl: Central DI is caused by deficient vasopressin release and responds to desmopressin.
objective: Differentiate central from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus by desmopressin response.

sources.title: Diabetes Insipidus
sources.support: NIDDK describes central DI as deficient vasopressin production or release.

sources.title: Diabetes insipidus
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes vasopressin deficiency and desmopressin response in central DI.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Medullary thyroid carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells and secretes calcitonin; hereditary forms are associated with RET activation.
vignette: A thyroid nodule biopsy shows nests of neuroendocrine cells and amyloid stroma. Serum calcitonin is markedly elevated.
lead: Which cell type gave rise to the tumor?
distractor_notes: Follicular cells give rise to papillary and follicular thyroid cancers and synthesize thyroid hormone.
Parathyroid chief cells produce PTH.
Pituitary thyrotrophs produce TSH.
Adrenal chromaffin cells produce catecholamines and give rise to pheochromocytoma.
key_expl: Medullary thyroid carcinoma derives from calcitonin-producing parafollicular C cells.
objective: Identify the cellular origin of medullary thyroid carcinoma.

sources.title: Medullary thyroid cancer
sources.support: NCI describes medullary thyroid cancer as arising from C cells and producing calcitonin.

sources.title: Multiple endocrine neoplasia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics links medullary thyroid carcinoma to RET-related MEN2.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Autonomous aldosterone excess increases distal sodium reabsorption and potassium/hydrogen secretion, causing hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and suppressed renin.
vignette: A 44-year-old man has resistant hypertension, muscle weakness, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, high aldosterone, and suppressed renin.
distractors: Secondary hyperaldosteronism from renal artery stenosis
distractor_notes: Renal artery stenosis causes elevated renin as well as aldosterone.
Primary adrenal insufficiency causes hypotension and hyperkalemia.
SIADH causes hyponatremia without hypokalemic alkalosis.
Pheochromocytoma causes catecholamine excess rather than suppressed-renin aldosterone excess.
key_expl: High aldosterone with low renin and hypokalemic hypertension indicates primary hyperaldosteronism.
objective: Recognize primary hyperaldosteronism from renin-aldosterone physiology.

sources.title: Primary Aldosteronism
sources.support: NIDDK describes autonomous aldosterone excess causing hypertension and low potassium with low renin.

sources.title: Hyperaldosteronism
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes aldosterone excess and hypokalemic hypertension.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Catecholamine-secreting chromaffin-cell tumors cause episodic adrenergic surges with headache, sweating, palpitations, and hypertension.
vignette: A 39-year-old woman has episodic pounding headaches, palpitations, diaphoresis, and severe paroxysmal hypertension.
distractor_notes: Primary hyperaldosteronism causes sustained hypertension and hypokalemia rather than catecholamine spells.
Panic attacks may mimic symptoms but do not explain severe recurrent hypertensive surges from catecholamine excess.
Hyperthyroidism causes more persistent adrenergic symptoms and thyroid abnormalities.
Cushing syndrome has chronic cortisol-excess features.
key_expl: Paroxysmal hypertension with headache, palpitations, and sweating is classic pheochromocytoma.
objective: Recognize pheochromocytoma from episodic catecholamine symptoms.

sources.title: Pheochromocytoma
sources.support: NCI describes pheochromocytoma as a catecholamine-secreting tumor causing hypertension and adrenergic symptoms.

sources.title: Pheochromocytoma
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes episodic headache, sweating, palpitations, and hypertension.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: PTH deficiency lowers renal calcium reabsorption and calcitriol activation while increasing phosphate retention, causing hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia.
vignette: After total thyroidectomy, a patient develops perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm. Calcium is low and phosphate is high.
lead: Which hormone deficiency most directly explains these findings?
distractor_notes: Calcitonin deficiency does not cause postoperative hypocalcemic tetany.
Aldosterone deficiency causes hyperkalemia and hypotension.
Cortisol deficiency causes adrenal insufficiency.
GH deficiency does not produce acute hypocalcemia.
key_expl: Post-thyroidectomy hypocalcemia with hyperphosphatemia indicates loss of parathyroid function and PTH.

sources.title: Hypoparathyroidism
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes hypoparathyroidism after neck surgery with hypocalcemia.

sources.title: Hypoparathyroidism
sources.support: NIDDK describes PTH deficiency causing low calcium and high phosphate.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Absolute insulin deficiency plus counterregulatory hormones accelerates lipolysis and hepatic ketogenesis, producing high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
vignette: A 17-year-old with type 1 diabetes has abdominal pain, vomiting, Kussmaul respirations, glucose 480 mg/dL, and positive serum ketones.
lead: Which metabolic pathway is most directly increased?
correct: Hepatic ketone body production from fatty acids
distractors: Malonyl-CoA inhibition of fatty acid entry into mitochondria
distractor_notes: Glycogen synthesis is reduced during severe insulin deficiency.
Peripheral glucose uptake falls, contributing to hyperglycemia.
Low insulin favors fatty acid oxidation rather than malonyl-CoA-mediated inhibition.
Lipolysis is increased, not inhibited.
key_expl: Insulin deficiency increases adipose lipolysis and hepatic ketogenesis, causing ketoacidosis.
objective: Explain DKA through increased lipolysis and ketone production.

sources.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes DKA as severe insulin deficiency causing ketone accumulation and acidosis.

sources.title: Diabetes Overview
sources.support: NIDDK describes insulin as central to glucose utilization and metabolic control.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Implantation outside the uterine cavity, most often in a fallopian tube, can cause unilateral pelvic pain and life-threatening intra-abdominal bleeding if rupture occurs.
vignette: A 29-year-old woman with 7 weeks of amenorrhea has unilateral pelvic pain and spotting. Pregnancy test is positive, and serum beta-hCG is above the expected transvaginal-ultrasound discriminatory level. Ultrasound shows no intrauterine gestational sac and identifies a separate adnexal gestational sac.
distractor_notes: Threatened intrauterine abortion requires an intrauterine pregnancy; here beta-hCG is above the discriminatory level and ultrasound shows a separate extrauterine gestational sac.
Ovarian torsion can cause unilateral pain but does not explain a separate extrauterine gestational sac in a pregnant patient.
PID does not explain pregnancy findings.
With beta-hCG above the discriminatory level, absence of an intrauterine sac plus a separate adnexal gestational sac is not a normal early intrauterine pregnancy.
key_expl: Positive pregnancy with no intrauterine gestation and an adnexal mass strongly indicates ectopic pregnancy.
objective: Recognize ectopic pregnancy from early-pregnancy pain and ultrasound findings.
clues: positive pregnancy with beta-hCG above the ultrasound discriminatory level
separate adnexal gestational sac with no intrauterine pregnancy

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Abnormal placentation and maternal endothelial dysfunction after 20 weeks cause hypertension with proteinuria or systemic organ injury.
vignette: A 31-year-old woman at 33 weeks gestation has new blood pressure of 168/108 mm Hg, headache, and proteinuria.
distractor_notes: Chronic hypertension predates pregnancy or begins before 20 weeks and does not inherently cause new proteinuria.
Gestational diabetes causes hyperglycemia, not hypertensive proteinuric disease.
Placenta previa causes painless vaginal bleeding.
Hyperemesis occurs earlier with severe vomiting.
key_expl: New hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria and neurologic symptoms is preeclampsia.
objective: Recognize preeclampsia from gestational timing and end-organ findings.

sources.title: Preeclampsia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes preeclampsia as new hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or organ dysfunction.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Failure of testicular descent leaves the testis outside the scrotum, increasing risks of impaired spermatogenesis and testicular malignancy.
vignette: A 1-year-old boy has an undescended right testis palpable in the inguinal canal.
lead: Which long-term risk is increased if the condition remains uncorrected?
distractor_notes: Cryptorchidism is specifically associated with testicular cancer risk, not prostate cancer.
Bladder cancer risk is unrelated.
Renal cell carcinoma is unrelated.
Adrenal cortical carcinoma is unrelated.
key_expl: Undescended testes carry increased risk of infertility and testicular germ cell cancer.
objective: Recognize major long-term complications of cryptorchidism.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes increased infertility and testicular cancer risk with cryptorchidism.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Ovarian follicular depletion lowers estrogen and inhibin production, removing negative feedback and increasing pituitary FSH and LH, especially FSH.
vignette: A 52-year-old woman has 14 months of amenorrhea and hot flashes.
lead: Which hormonal pattern is most expected?
distractors: Low FSH with low LH from pituitary suppression
High inhibin B with low FSH
distractor_notes: Menopause is ovarian failure, so estrogen falls and FSH rises.
Progesterone is not persistently elevated after loss of ovulation.
Pituitary gonadotropins rise because negative feedback is reduced.
Inhibin falls rather than rises.
key_expl: Follicular depletion lowers estrogen and inhibin, causing hypergonadotropic ovarian failure.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: BRCA1 participates in homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks; germline loss increases breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility.
vignette: A 34-year-old woman with triple-negative breast cancer has a mother and sister with early breast cancer and a maternal aunt with ovarian cancer. Germline testing shows a pathogenic BRCA1 variant.
correct: Homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks
distractor_notes: Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome.
Nucleotide excision repair defects cause xeroderma pigmentosum.
UV thymine dimers are repaired mainly by nucleotide excision in humans, not BRCA1.
BRCA1 has major DNA repair and tumor suppressor roles beyond RNA splicing.
key_expl: BRCA1 is essential for high-fidelity homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks.
objective: Connect BRCA1 cancer susceptibility with homologous recombination deficiency.
clues: family history of breast and ovarian cancer

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Germ cell malignancies commonly present as painless testicular masses in young men and are associated with cryptorchidism as a risk factor.
vignette: A 27-year-old man notices a painless firm intratesticular mass that does not transilluminate.
distractor_notes: Hydroceles are fluid collections that usually transilluminate.
Varicoceles feel like a bag of worms and are extratesticular.
Epididymitis is painful and inflammatory.
Inguinal hernias are reducible groin/scrotal protrusions rather than firm intratesticular masses.
key_expl: A painless firm intratesticular mass in a young man should be considered testicular cancer until proven otherwise.
objective: Recognize the classic presentation of a testicular germ cell tumor.
